title: postfix ! inside a durable body means 'unwrap this Action step', so applying it to anything that is not a compiler-bound Action.run(...) is refused rather than read as TypeScript's non-null assertion

diagnostics.messageContains: postfix ! is supported only directly on a compiler-bound Action.run(...) Result

notes: specification/durable-execution.mdx §Durable Boundary Contract, read with ':63' ('Property access and argument passing on a symbolic result MUST create typed projections and dependency edges when representable in Plan IR') and ':71' ('The compiler MUST reject an operation that would inspect a symbolic value without a corresponding IR representation'). Inside a durable body postfix ! is not TypeScript's non-null assertion: it is the subset's spelling of 'unwrap this Action's Result and make the step it names a dependency of what follows'. There is no Plan IR node for 'assert this is not null', so accepting the operator on a non-Action operand would either drop it silently or persist a dependency edge to a step that never existed. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: SMITHERS4112 is enforced by both implementations and was declared by nothing until this case, for the same reason as its sibling — step 11 rewrote the cases that used to declare it into acceptances. THIS IS NOT THE RULE THE OLD CASES DECLARED, and the distinction is recorded in the implementations themselves. The withdrawn SMITHERS4112 was WALL 6, the fallthrough where 'every call the Plan could not name — including Capability.context() — landed'; that is gone and now throws PlanUnrepresentable (poc/src/durable/source-compiler.ts:1588, compiler/forkbridge/durable.go.txt:1235). The comment at the reference's withdrawal names what stayed: 'The two SMITHERS4112 refusals above it, on postfix ! and on an unresolvable run receiver, are separate rules and stay.' This case declares the first of those two. THE DECLARED POSITION: 15:25 is the operand `input.key!`, the expression carrying the operator. Both backends report the same code, the same position and the same sentence; Backend agreement is 1/1 and no marker is needed. A PROGRAM THIS CASE DELIBERATELY IS NOT, and it is worth recording because the first draft was exactly it: spelling the input `{ key: string | undefined }` instead of `{ key: string }` makes the two backends DIVERGE — the reference still reports SMITHERS4112@15:25, but the fork refuses earlier with SMITHERS4110@14:30 at the arrow function, because an optional field is not a durable codec type and the fork checks the boundary contract before it lowers the body. That is a real, pre-existing ordering difference between the two implementations, unrelated to this rule, and it was measured rather than reasoned about. The non-optional spelling removes it and leaves the postfix-! rule as the only thing the case can be answering. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed — see this revision's report: the reference's report site was deleted and this case turned red; the declared code and column were each mutated and it turned red on BOTH backends; the file was restored and sha256-compared byte-identical after every mutation.
